SettingsPresetInfo: Export the current settings as a .masselguard file. SettingsTrustedNetInfo: These SSIDs are treated as safe. Turn protection on by adding a 'Trusted networks' rule in the WiFi rules list (there you also pick which tunnel to bring up on untrusted networks).
SettingsTrustedListDesc: One SSID per line. The whole list shares a single action, set by the Trusted networks rule: the tunnel comes up on any other (untrusted) network and disconnects on these.
RuleDialogTimeInvalid: Enter valid start and end times in HH:mm format.

TunnelMetadataInfo: This tunnel is managed by the WireGuard app. Only group assignment and notes can be edited here — connection settings are stored in the WireGuard profile.
TunnelDialogNotesHint: Optional. Shown as a tooltip on the tunnel name.
TunnelDialogDataCapsHint: Warn (log, tray, row highlight) and optionally disconnect (‘Kill at cap’) when usage crosses a threshold. 0 = off. A cap adds a usage ring to the tunnel's row (inner = day, middle = week, outer = month). Usage is estimated from connection history and is not exact — MasselGUARD is not responsible for inaccurate reporting, or for tunnels being disconnected (or not) as a result.
SplitSectionHint: Choose which destination IP ranges go through this tunnel. Local tunnels only.
SplitModeOff: Off — route everything through the tunnel
SplitModeExclude: Exclude these ranges (full tunnel except the list)
SplitModeInclude: Only these ranges (everything else bypasses the tunnel)
SplitRangesHint: One per line, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24 or 10.0.0.5. IPv4 and IPv6 supported.
SplitAppsComingSoon: Per-app split tunneling arrives in a later 4.x update.
SplitInvalidRange: "{0}" is not a valid IP range. Use CIDR notation like 192.168.1.0/24.
CapConnectConfirmMsg: You have reached the data cap for "{0}" ({1} of {2}). Connect anyway and ignore the limit?
TunnelScriptsInfo: Run a .bat or .ps1 file (or embed a script inline) before or after a tunnel connects or disconnects. Scripts run as the current user. Exit code 0 = success.
SettingsRulesInfo: Map a WiFi network name (SSID) to a tunnel. When you connect to that network MasselGUARD automatically activates the tunnel. Leave the tunnel empty to disconnect all tunnels on that network.
SettingsDefaultActionInfo: Choose what happens when you connect to a network that has no matching rule.
SettingsOpenWifiInfo: Automatically activates a tunnel whenever you connect to an open (passwordless) WiFi network — before any rule is evaluated. This protects you on public hotspots.
SettingsGroupsDesc: Organise tunnels into collapsible sections. Drag ↑↓ to reorder. Tunnels not assigned to a group appear under Ungrouped.
SettingsDisableWifiRulesDesc: When on, WiFi rules and the default action are not applied. Connect and disconnect tunnels manually.
SettingsDnsLeakInfo: On a split-tunnel WireGuard connection, Windows can send DNS queries out adapters other than the tunnel, leaking them to the local Wi-Fi/router resolver instead of the tunnel resolver — so DNS-based filtering and ad-blocking stop working. The two machine-wide Windows policies below close that gap; for full protection, disable both. Local network access is unaffected.
SettingsDnsLeakSmartDesc: Windows sends each DNS query out all active adapters at once and takes the first answer. Disable to keep DNS on the tunnel resolver.
SettingsDnsLeakParallelDesc: Windows looks up IPv4 (A) and IPv6 (AAAA) at the same time, which can leak the AAAA query. Disable to query them sequentially (slightly slower).
SettingsDnsLeakWarnDesc: How to alert you when an active tunnel may be leaking DNS and protection is off. Turn all three off to disable. (The log and tray alerts stay silent once smart name resolution is disabled above.)
SettingsDnsLeakStatusOff: Enabled — Windows default (DNS may leak on split tunnels).
SettingsDnsLeakReboot: Reconnect your tunnel for changes to take effect — a reboot guarantees it. These are global Windows settings, not per-tunnel.
SettingsDnsLeakAppliedMsg: DNS setting updated. Reconnect your tunnel (or reboot) for it to fully take effect.
SettingsWireGuardDesc: Open WireGuard GUI or view the WireGuard service log
TooltipQuickConnect: Open a .conf file and connect instantly — no import needed
ModeStandaloneDesc: Manages tunnels directly using tunnel.dll + wireguard.dll next to the exe. No WireGuard app required. Tunnels are stored and encrypted locally.
ModeCompanionDesc: Works alongside the official WireGuard for Windows app. Automates connecting and disconnecting your existing WireGuard tunnels based on WiFi rules.
ModeMixedDesc: Both modes active. Manage your own local tunnels AND automate the WireGuard app tunnels side by side.
SettingsSuppressUpdatePrompt: Don't ask to update the installed version at startup
WizardWelcomeBody:
MasselGUARD automatically activates WireGuard tunnels based on your WiFi network.

This wizard takes about a minute. You can re-run it anytime from Settings.
WizardLangBody: Choose your language and preferred colour scheme.

WizardDoneBody: MasselGUARD is configured and ready. Add tunnels and WiFi rules from the main window.
WizardRulesBody: MasselGUARD uses rules to decide which tunnel to activate when your network changes. You configure rules in Settings after this wizard.
WizardRulesWifiHint: — map a WiFi network name (SSID) to a tunnel
WizardRulesDefaultHint: — what to do when no rule matches
WizardRulesOpenHint: — force a tunnel on passwordless WiFi, before any rule
WizardRulesWhy: Typical use: VPN off on your trusted home network, on automatically everywhere else.
WizardManualBody: MasselGUARD can switch tunnels automatically when your WiFi network changes.

OrphansDescription: Running WireGuardTunnel$ services that MasselGUARD did not start in this session — usually left over from an improper shutdown. Scan to detect and stop them.
